=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel — Buyer-Side Review of Seller's Draft

Below is my assessment for each issue. Baseline: AUD 24,000,000; 100% of Paperbark Analytics; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law. All seller positions are drafting from the *other side* and should be read sceptically.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** Aggregate cap of 20% of price = AUD 4.8m for general warranty claims.
- **Buyer wants:** Higher general cap (commonly 25–50% of price for a private software deal of this size), with any W&I insurance interacting cleanly.
- **Recommendation:** Push to ≥30% (AUD 7.2m), or explore W&I insurance given disclosed risk clusters — *4.8m is thin against Bluefen/Riverlark/privacy exposure.*

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- **Seller:** Per-claim de minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k; only the excess above basket recoverable ("deductible" style).
- **Buyer wants:** Lower thresholds, and a "first-dollar/tipping" basket (once tripped, recover from dollar one), not a deductible.
- **Recommendation:** Accept modest de minimis but convert basket to tipping and reduce toward ~AUD 120k (0.5%) — *deductible basket silently transfers the first 250k of loss to the buyer.*

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months; and "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer wants:** At least 24 months (past two audit cycles) for general warranties; and reject the catch-all that sweeps every claim type into the shortest regime.
- **Recommendation:** 24 months general; **strike** the "applies to all Claims" default — *the sweep clause is the real trap, not the 18 months itself.*

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the *same* cap and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** Title/capacity warranties capped at 100% of price and surviving 6–7 years (or statutory limitation).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject** — carve fundamentals out to 100% cap / long survival — *you are buying the shares; if title fails you can lose everything but recover only 4.8m.*

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** Silent — no express fraud carve-out; limitations drafted to apply "to all Claims of any nature" (9.3/12.8/20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** Express carve-out so caps, time limits, baskets, knowledge and exclusive-remedy provisions do **not** apply to fraud, wilful concealment or wilful default.
- **Recommendation:** **Insert fraud/wilful-default carve-out across all limitation clauses** — *absent this, the "all Claims" language purports to cap even the seller's own fraud (and is likely void but should not be litigated).*

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** Deemed general disclosure of the entire data room plus Accounts, statutory registers and all publicly searchable records (1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Disclosure limited to matters *fairly and specifically* disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature/scope of the issue; no sweep of public registers.
- **Recommendation:** **Require "fair disclosure" standard; strike deemed disclosure of public records** — *blanket data-room disclosure guts the warranties by making every buried document a defence.*

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer/advisers knew or that was *discoverable* from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** At most, exclusion only for matters of *actual* knowledge of named deal-team individuals; no "constructive/discoverable" knowledge; no imputation of adviser knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "discoverable"; limit to actual knowledge of named persons** — *"discoverable" combined with sweep disclosure means you warrant nothing you could theoretically have found.*

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** "Reasonable endeavours"; condition deemed satisfied on delivery of counterparty consent; no final consent or satisfied conditions in data room yet (Disclosure §2).
- **Buyer wants:** Bluefen written consent (with its 11.3 conditions actually satisfied) as a hard Condition Precedent to Completion — it's ~30% of FY26 revenue.
- **Recommendation:** **Make satisfied written consent a true CP; upgrade to "best endeavours"** — *losing a 30%-revenue customer at change of control is a core value driver, not an endeavours obligation.*

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m to be released *after* Completion; change-of-control and discharge clauses unaddressed; not yet repaid (Disclosure §3).
- **Buyer wants:** On a debt-free/cash-free deal, Riverlark repaid and security **discharged at or before Completion**, evidenced by a payoff letter / deed of release.
- **Recommendation:** **Require discharge as a Completion deliverable (or price reduction + escrow)** — *post-Completion release leaves the company you own encumbered and breaches debt-free/cash-free; this is a ~3.2m price point.*

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 DD-005 Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller," not in the funds flow; on-costs (payroll tax/super) unstated (Disclosure §5).
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses triggered by Completion are a seller/pre-Completion liability — borne by Seller, including on-costs, via specific indemnity or funds-flow adjustment.
- **Recommendation:** **Allocate the 420k + on-costs to Seller as a leakage/indemnity item** — *Completion-triggered bonuses are seller consideration, not your post-Completion cost.*

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; "adequate." DD-010 shows AUD 180k open; IP transfers only on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees (Disclosure §4).
- **Buyer wants:** Indemnity covering the risk that **IP/Project Materials do not vest** (loss of IP, re-procurement, infringement), not merely the 180k fee; plus evidence of payment and confirmatory assignment as a deliverable.
- **Recommendation:** **Broaden indemnity to IP-title failure and require proof of payment + assignment at Completion** — *the real exposure is losing the IP, which dwarfs the 180k fee.*

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- **Seller:** DD-006 "preliminary," not characterised as a breach, no loss stated; ~1,240 records sent to wrong external address.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific indemnity for the incident (notification/regulatory costs under Privacy Act / OAIC, remediation, third-party claims) uncapped by the general regime, plus seller conduct of/ cooperation on the investigation.
- **Recommendation:** **Obtain a specific, carved-out indemnity for the incident** — *an eligible data breach triggers mandatory notification and regulatory risk; "preliminary" is seller spin, not a waiver.*

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three related renewals AUD 110k each (AUD 330k) are "ordinary-course operating costs"; terminability/accrual unstated (Disclosure §8).
- **Buyer wants:** Clarity on whether these are committed/unavoidable; on a cash-free/debt-free basis, pre-Completion committed spend should be reflected in working capital/price or warranted as ordinary course.
- **Recommendation:** **Confirm terminability and treat committed portion as a price/WC adjustment** — *"ordinary course" is asserted, not evidenced; 330k of locked-in spend affects value.*

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply uniformly "to all Claims of any nature" (9.3/12.8/20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** Distinct regimes — general warranties vs. fundamentals/title vs. tax vs. specific indemnities vs. fraud — each with its own cap/time limit; indemnities not subject to warranty limitations.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject uniform treatment; separate the limitation architecture by claim category** — *a single regime lets the weakest (general) limits swallow your strongest protections.*

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title evidenced solely by the share register at DD-012; notes Buyer hasn't verified (Disclosure §10).
- **Buyer wants:** An unqualified title/capacity warranty (100% unencumbered, fully paid, no third-party rights/options), independent of the register, backed by the fundamental regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Insist on a hard title warranty + ASIC/register checks; do not rely on seller-produced register** — *the disclosure is pre-positioning to blame your lack of verification; the warranty must carry the risk.*

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP "settled under the general regime" — i.e. subject to general cap/18-month limit.
- **Buyer wants:** A **tax indemnity/deed** covering pre-Completion periods with survival to at least 5–7 years (statutory assessment period) and separate cap; IP warranties with longer survival and no knowledge/disclosure dilution.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject folding tax/IP into the general regime; add tax deed with statutory-period survival** — *tax audits surface well beyond 18 months; a general cap/time limit leaves pre-Completion tax uncovered.*

---

### Cross-cutting priorities (my top asks)
1. **Fraud carve-out** (SPA-N-005) and **fair-disclosure + actual-knowledge** fixes (006/007) — these three neutralise the seller's broadest value-destroying moves.
2. **Riverlark discharge at Completion** (009) and **Bluefen CP** (008) — the two largest discrete value items (~3.2m debt; ~30% revenue).
3. **Fundamentals/title/tax carve-outs** from the general regime (004/014/016).
4. **Specific indemnities** for the privacy incident (012), Ironquay IP (011) and employee bonuses (010).

If helpful, I can turn this into a mark-up issues list / negotiation tracker with fallback positions for each. Note one factual flag for the deal team: the **DD-005 bonuses (420k)** and **Riverlark (3.2m)** together are material against a 4.8m cap — worth modelling before you concede on SPA-N-001.

*This is deal-support analysis, not a formal legal opinion; please have NSW-qualified counsel settle the final drafting.*
